notes:
Account background: mid-market SaaS building a customer support assistant (multi-tenant). Currently on OpenAI for chat + embeddings; experimenting with moving serving to Redwood to lock predictable capacity and lower unit cost. Primary drivers: cost predictability, VPC/Dedicated for customer data isolation, better observability into per-route token costs.

POC scope: 14-day hosted POC -> evaluate parity + cost -> Dedicated sizing discussion if POC passes. We shipped a compatibility shim to map their existing OpenAI calls to Redwood request shape; main concerns are: 
- Prompt parity: behavior differences for a few system prompts (company names, multi-turn context) — Amberfall runs nightly evals and flagged ~6% deviance on NLU intents.
- Function calling: incumbent supports nested function outputs; need to validate Redwood's function-calling semantics and how errors/partial outputs stream.
- Token accounting mismatch: their finance team sees a billing delta vs OpenAI due to different tokenization and stop-token handling. Asked for token breakdown per-request in console.
- Regressions: Amberfall wants a runbook + assistance porting their regression harness (pytest + eval dataset ~25k prompts). SE Marco offered a mapping guide and to run a joint regression run.

Security/compliance: SOC2 required for production, SSO/SAML integration mandatory, KMS for key management. Also asked about contractual data residency for EU customers — will require Dedicated in EU region or Private. Legal awaiting DPA redlines (linked SEC-1192).

Pricing/Commercial: Amberfall is cost-sensitive; target is ~30% unit-cost reduction vs incumbent. Forecasting ~$90k-$150k ARR if Dedicated pricing matches unit economics and initial regressions are resolved. They prefer monthly billing cadence during POC and then committed monthly/annual for Dedicated.
